title: regional capacity scouting journal - 2028-03-12
body:
Purpose:
Quick working journal from today’s regional-capacity scouting session. This is a lightweight capture of what we observed, experiments we kicked off, and immediate follow-ups. Not a formal playbook — think of it as the real-time scout notes that feed the next capacity readout.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Marco Reynolds (ops)
- Liang Chen (pool scheduling)
- Noah Rivera (SRE)
- Joined briefly: Priya S (solutions eng)

Agenda (30m):
1) Morning telemetry check + surprising deltas
2) Candidate regions for soft-reserve buckets this week
3) Pre-warm / probe allocation experiment plan
4) Action items + quick decisions (10m)

Top-line observation:
- Overall fleet utilization is 72% across committed pools. We saw an unusual thread of long-lived KV-cache heavy requests in eu-north between 03:10-03:45 UTC that drove per-node memory into occasional throttles and bumped tail latency for 8 minutes. No customer SLA breaches reported, but traces show >2x token lat spikes for smaller prompt sizes.

Region-by-region quick notes:
1) us-west-2 (primary consumer of hosted API)
- Capacity snapshot (12:00 PDT): available GPUs 36 / total dedicated 64 (56% free-ish if you only count burstable slots).
- Observed trend: burst capacity consumption trending +15% weekdays 10:00-12:00 local.
- Risk: preemptible backfills were delayed for 18 minutes due to a scheduling backoff bug (see INFRA-2741). Patch queued in PR #4128.
- Short decision: hold one soft-reserve row of 8 GPUs active from 09:30-13:30 PDT M-F for next 2 weeks to smooth morning spikes. Action: Marco to annotate reservation label and run quota bump (due 2028-03-14).

2) eu-north
- Capacity snapshot (12:00 CET): available GPUs 14 / total 44 (low headroom).
- Incident: KV-cache heavy stream (see traces) — appears correlated with a small subset of customers on model-variant: gptx-small-ql. We believe a recent client rollout changed prefix behavior.
- Mitigation: added temporary routing rule to direct that customer’s traffic to a compatible quantized variant (gptx-small-q8) for 3 hours; tail latency recovered.
- Follow-up: Liang to add a property to model-catalog entries that surfaces 'kv-cache-risk' flag before rollouts. Jira: INFRA-2746 (owner Liang).

3) ap-southeast-1 (edge / partner region)
- Capacity snapshot (SGT): available GPUs 8 / total 16 (tight).
- Note: partner integration testing scheduled for 2028-03-20 — recommend bumping priming window and adding two warm nodes 48h prior.
- Experiment: started a 'probe allocation' job to send canonical short prompts from warm nodes to confirm KV cache hit amplification; initial results (1h) show 28% token-cost improvement after prefill.
- Action: Noah to capture probe-job logs to evidence cost delta for partner proposal (due 2028-03-16).

Surge readiness and hedging notes:
- Probability window for an external API-driven surge (marketing sandbox) next Tuesday 2028-03-19 estimated at 22% (based on historical correlation with scheduled demos).
- Proposed hedging approach: soft-reserve buckets in us-west-2 (8 GPUs) + 4 GPU burst in eu-north (on-call carve) triggered by the surge signal pipeline (signal: sudden 60% delta in 5m rolling RPS).
- We will not preempt customer dedicated pools without a 2-hour heads-up; instead prefer model-variant fallback + routing policy changes.

Pre-warm / probe experiment (notes):
- Objective: quantify tail-latency improvement vs cost delta for different prefill lengths (10s, 30s, 2min) and different sequence-length profiles.
- Setup: 3 cohorts across us-west-2 small GPU row: cohort A (no prefill), B (30s warm), C (2min warm). Each cohort receives 300 canonical test prompts/hour for next 48h.
- Early observation (first 90m): 30s warm reduces 95th percentile token latency by ~18% for short prompts; 2min warm only marginally better (+3%) vs 30s for heavy KV patterns.
- Note-to-self: compute per-token amortized cost and add to Optimize backlog.

Runbook quick wins (things we can flip in 10-30m):
- Add 'kv-cache-risk' tag to model-catalog entries (small infra change).
- Add a temporary routing override for the EU customer that caused kv-heavy behavior (done).
- Add probe-job CI job to infra repo so we can re-run quickly on demand (PR drafted).

Unresolved questions / open threads:
- How to alert proactively for KV-cache pressure without generating noisy alerts? (threshold exploration needed).
- Should we expose a customer-facing best-practices doc for prefix usage? (Priya to draft a short FAQ with examples).
- Is the morning surge pattern in us-west an increasing trend or an outlier? Need 2 more weeks of signals.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marco: label soft-reserve row + run quota bump for us-west-2 (8 GPUs) — due 2028-03-14.
- Liang: INFRA-2746: add 'kv-cache-risk' field to model-catalog schema + tests — due 2028-03-20.
- Noah: collect probe-job logs and attach cost analysis for partner pitch — due 2028-03-16.
- Priya: customer FAQ draft on prefix/prompt patterns (internal) — due 2028-03-18.
- Aisha: follow-up readout next scouting sync, include 48h pre-warm experiment results — due 2028-03-15.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the experiment cohorts small to avoid changing production economics; can scale if signal looks promising.
- Remember to record the exact environment (docker tag, kernel version) for the probe-job — past discrepancies made data noisy.
- Slack reference: see thread infra-capacity-scouts for raw logs (thread pinned).

Scratch/clippings:
- Quick query used: `select region, sum(allocated_gpus), sum(free_gpus) from fleet where timestamp > now() - interval '15m' group by region;`
- Example trace id: trace-eun-2028-03-12-03-19-AB12
- PR for scheduler backoff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4128

Next sync:
- Friday 2028-03-16, 09:00 PT — quick 20m sync to review cohort A/B/C after 48h of sampling and confirm hedging plan for partner test.

End of journal.

-- Aisha
